clue.text: Properly organized diets are most handy

indicators.note: the letters of the words are to be organized properly, put into a new order

explanation.surface: A nutritionist claims that diets arranged the right way are the most convenient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Properly organized' rearranges DIETS ARE; 'are' looks like the verb of the sentence but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being readiest means being the most prepared and closest to hand, so the most handy.

clue.text: Coppers always have a close look

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated P
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Police officers forever peering closely at things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but here it means copper coins, pennies (P). EER is e'er, poetry's shortening of 'ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look narrowly and searchingly at something.

clue.text: Reliable horses

explanation.surface: A dependable lot of horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady and dependable; a stable is also a collection of horses kept by one owner.

clue.text: Heartless fool — the second to make a splash

indicators.note: without its heart, the middle letter is taken out of the word for a fool

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool
the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: A brainless idiot is the next one to cause a big splash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle A from SAP to give SP. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To splatter is to splash liquid about messily, scattering drops.

clue.text: A greenhorn in need of kindly support

parts.note: tender means gentle and kindly
a foot supports the body, or is the base that holds something up

explanation.surface: A novice who needs gentle backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderfoot is a newcomer or novice unused to hardship, just as a greenhorn is an inexperienced beginner.

clue.text: A fireball from remote parts

indicators.note: the word is parted, broken up so its letters can be set in a new order

explanation.surface: A ball of fire arriving from far-off regions of space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun (distant parts) but is the anagram signal, a verb meaning 'splits up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a bright streak in the sky from space debris burning up; a very bright one is called a fireball.

clue.text: A salesman one feeding a duplicator

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
an eater is someone who feeds

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman who keeps the office copier supplied with paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is a device that repeats or reproduces something, such as a signal, so a duplicator.

clue.text: Talk in desultory fashion of a country walk

explanation.surface: Rambling chat about a walk in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramble is to talk aimlessly and at length; a ramble is also a leisurely stroll through the countryside.

clue.text: Sections of the city getting into convenience food

indicators.note: one piece gets into the middle of the other, so it is placed inside

parts.note: pies are a ready-made convenience food
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: Parts of the City of London where ready meals are taking hold.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district covering the City, London's financial square mile.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces are portions or parts of a whole, as sections are.

clue.text: Nothing is dumped beside the German waterway

indicators.note: one piece is set down right next to the other, so they sit side by side

parts.note: the figure zero, O, stands for nothing
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Rubbish thrown down next to a German canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oder is a river forming much of the border between Germany and Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a major central European river, so a waterway.

clue.text: Soldier and medico in council — that's right

indicators.note: the doctor's letters are placed in the council word

parts.note: a board is a governing council or committee
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A soldier and a doctor sitting on a committee, which is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' supplies IE, the abbreviation for id est, Latin for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardier is a non-commissioned rank in the artillery, so a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Secure the proceeds of salvage

indicators.note: the letters of the word are processed, and what comes out of that working is a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lock away the money made from salvaging a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proceeds' looks like money earned but signals that the letters of 'Secure' are worked into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage something is to save it from loss or wreckage, which is to rescue it.

clue.text: Secret communication engendering trust

explanation.surface: Sharing a secret builds trust.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidence is a secret told privately; confidence is also firm belief and reliance on someone.

clue.text: Came down before time with lines learned

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the next in the answer

parts.note: lit is past tense of light, to come down and settle, as a bird lit on a branch
an era is a period of time
RY, railway, gives lines in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone came downstairs early, having memorised their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: RY is the abbreviation for railway, here the lines a train runs on.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary describes someone well read and bookish, so learned in letters.

clue.text: Boy pinching girl gets beaten

indicators.note: the boy's name pinches the girl's, holding it inside

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lad nips a lass and gets a hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: To tan someone's hide is to thrash them, so tanned means beaten.

clue.text: Guts shown by a bird in nest-building

indicators.note: the bird is placed in the nest letters
the word nest is built up again from its letters in a new order

parts.note: a rail is a wading bird

explanation.surface: Innards on view as a bird puts together its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nest-building' reads as one compound, but 'building' rearranges the nest letters into ENTS, which 'in' opens around the bird; the rail is a marsh bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the internal organs, especially the intestines, which are the guts.

clue.text: Test for a non-specific factor in fish

indicators.note: the unknown quantity is placed in the fish

parts.note: the trout is a freshwater fish
in algebra y stands for an unknown, unspecified quantity

explanation.surface: Testing a fish for some unknown ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: Mathematicians use x and y for unknowns, so Y is a factor with no specific value.
explanation.definitionFit: A try-out is a trial run or audition, a test of someone's ability.

clue.text: Transport set-up the top man's following

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means written upwards, so the transport word is read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle for transport
the king is the top man in the land

explanation.surface: A transport network, established by the boss, is succeeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' looks like a noun meaning an arrangement; in this down clue it reverses CART to give TRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracking means trailing someone or something, following its path.

clue.text: A married woman about fifty gives a resentful toss of the head

definitions.text: gives a resentful toss of the head

indicators.note: the woman goes about, around, the number

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A wife of fifty tosses her head in indignation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to show anger or offence by drawing up the head and chin, like a reined-in horse.

clue.text: Case of wine college head sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the whole run of letters is turned and read backwards

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A case of wine is returned by the head of a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses RETSINA plus C, the first letter of 'college', giving CANISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a container, usually a round metal tin, so a case.

clue.text: Italian capital raised — nearly all quite unethical

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means written upwards, so the capital is read backwards

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name of Rome, Italy's capital

indicators.note: nearly all of the word is kept, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: The Italian capital up in arms, with almost everyone completely immoral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ROMA into AMOR in this down clue; 'nearly' cuts the last letter from 'all' to give AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means having no moral principles at all, so lacking any ethics.

clue.text: A snooker player at the bar?

definitions.text: A snooker player at the bar?

parts.words: A snooker player at the bar?
parts.note: one who pots balls at a snooker table, reread as the worker in a pub who collects drinking vessels

explanation.surface: A snooker player propping up the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A potman is a pub worker who collects glasses (or pots); a snooker player pots balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub employee who gathers and washes the pots and glasses is the man of the pots.

clue.text: Composed, though in prison

explanation.surface: Written while locked up, like many a prison memoir.
explanation.definitionFit: Penned means written with a pen; it also means shut in a pen, confined like a prisoner.

clue.text: Green roads set off this very pleasant area

indicators.note: the letters are set off, sent off into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Leafy lanes show off a lovely spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' looks like 'enhance' but rearranges GREEN ROADS. A rose garden is a byword for a delightful place.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden planted with roses is a typically delightful spot, a pleasant area.

clue.text: Begs for some task — some useful task

indicators.note: only some of the words are used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Pleads for a chore, preferably a worthwhile chore.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'task — some'; the repetition of 'task' disguises the run.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for something is to request or beg for it.

clue.text: Writing a note, a man can give pain

parts.note: C is a musical note
he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man putting a letter on paper may suffer an ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing' is a link: write down A and the note C, then add HE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull, continuous pain.

clue.text: Split up a lot

explanation.surface: Divide up one batch.
explanation.definitionFit: To parcel out is to divide into portions; a parcel is also a lot, a batch of goods at auction.

clue.text: Help net a wild animal

indicators.note: wild letters run free and are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Lend a hand trapping a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' looks like it describes the animal but rearranges HELP NET A.
explanation.definitionFit: The elephant is a large animal with a trunk.
